epic.title: EPIC-051: Show the Brands Behind Others
epic.functionalNeed:
The Share of Voice donut shows the top 10 brands and puts the rest in one Others slice, and today hovering that slice only shows its name. On a category with many small brands, Others can be one of the largest slices and the user has no way to know what is inside it, not in the app and not in the exports.

The goal is to list the brands behind Others in the donut tooltip, to give the full Share of Voice list in the Excel export, and to name Others in the PowerPoint and PDF donut, where today it is a grey slice with no label. This was story 1.8 of GEO-678. It does not depend on natural answers, but it needs the Share of Voice formula of GEO-1556 (see Dependencies). [CHANGED 2026-11-05]
scope: GEO-1588 STORY-51.1: List the brands in the Others tooltip
GEO-1589 STORY-51.2: Give the full Share of Voice list in the Excel export
GEO-1590 STORY-51.3: Name Others in the PowerPoint and PDF donut
GEO-1587 STORY-51.4: Serve every brand behind Others from the Share of Voice distribution

scopeBoundaries.Dependencies:
- GEO-1556 (story 50.7 of GEO-678). With the formula live today, each answer counts 10 positions even when it names fewer or more brands, so the Share of Voice of all brands does not add up to 100% and Others can never be the exact sum of its brands. GEO-1556 changes the formula so all brands add up to 100% on every analysis date. US 1.1 AC3 can only pass once it ships. [CHANGED 2026-11-05]
- The full brand list behind Others. Today the app only receives the top 10 brands and Others is computed as what is left, so the brands inside it never reach the app. The tooltip, the deck line and the Excel table need every brand with its Share of Voice and the brand count, from the same data as the donut. [NEW 2026-11-05]

outOfScope: A full Share of Voice table slide in the deck: the full list lives in the Excel export
Any change to the Share of Voice formula (GEO-678 owns it)
One decimal in the tooltip, the deck line and the Excel table: Share of Voice stays in whole numbers as today [NEW 2026-11-05]
The free Lite analysis: its Share of Voice donut keeps today's behaviour [NEW 2026-11-05]

technicalAcceptanceCriteria.text: **TAC1** — With `others` of 48 brands: hovering the Others arc shows the header « Others 58% », « 48 brands », exactly 10 rows in the received order, and « and 38 more brands, see the export ».
**TAC2** — With `others` of 6 brands: 6 rows, no overflow line, no second divider.
**TAC3** — With `others` of 1 brand: « 1 brand » (singular); with 11: « and 1 more brand, see the export ».

**TAC4** — Focusing the Others legend button with Tab opens the tooltip; Escape closes it; focusing the Others arc opens it too and shows the blue outline; the svg has `role="group"` and the arc `role="button"` with its label.
**TAC5** — A brand at 0.3 % in `others.brands` shows « ~0% »; the tracked brand in `others.brands` has the same markup as the others.

**TAC6** — The header % equals the Others legend item % and the slice label (GEO-1528 value), including the case where `Math.round(others.sov)` differs from it by 1; when the GEO-1528 value is 0 with the slice drawn, all three read « ~0% ».
**TAC7** — Without `others` (Lite), or with `others.sov` ≤ 0.05 (no slice), the Others arc and legend item have no `tabIndex`, no button, no tooltip; all 22 existing tests stay green unchanged.
**TAC8** — The `side` passed to `SovOthersTooltip`: arc `right` on the neutral card, `left` on the branded card; legend item `top` in both.
**TAC9** — Hovering a brand slice still shows the name pill; hovering Others does not when the tooltip is active, and still does without `others` (Lite).
**TAC10** — `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint:i18n` and `pnpm test` green; the four locale files have the same new keys (parity test).
**TAC11** — Hovering the Others arc opens the tooltip and the `<path>` gets `aria-describedby` (Radix `asChild` on SVG works).

**TAC12** — (PM 2026-11-10, 875646) With `others.brandCount` = 1,427: header « 1,427 brands » and « and 1,417 more brands, see the export » (FR « 1 427 marques » / « et 1 417 autres marques, voir l'export », ES « 1.427 marcas » / « y 1.417 marcas más, ver la exportación »), the Others arc label too; same numbers as the Excel table and the deck line.

technicalAcceptanceCriteria.text: **DAC1 — Layout (frame 2.1):** Given an overview sheet, When it is generated, Then the ranking table is in columns A–E (Rank, Brand, Visibility %, Avg Position, AI Choice %), column F is empty and the Share of Voice table is in G–I (Rank, Brand, Share of Voice %), both starting on the same row (the section-title row)

**DAC2 — Styles:** Given the Share of Voice table, When it is generated, Then its title row « Share of Voice » uses the sub-section style of « Brand ranking », its header row the table-header style, and the tracked brand row the ranking table's highlight (yellow-50, the workbook's styles win — design comment 875353); cells left-aligned like every % cell of the workbook
**DAC3 — Category sheet (frame 2.2):** Given a category sheet, When it is generated, Then it has the same two tables for the category scope

**TAC1** — Given an overview sheet with 48 brands in scope, When it is generated, Then the ranking table is in A–E (10 rows, no SOV column, ordered by Visibility % desc, rank 1..10), F is empty on those rows, the SOV table is in G–I with 48 rows in the distribution's order, rank 1..48, title « Share of Voice » on exactly the ranking title's row

**TAC2** — Given an export with or without a period, When the SOV table is generated, Then its values come from the same service call and the same snapshots as the dashboard distribution of the same scope
**TAC3** — Given the tracked brand, When both tables are generated, Then its row is highlighted in both tables, every flagged row when several are; unbranded workbook: no highlight in the SOV table
**TAC4** — Given brands at 0.3 %, 0.00 and 12.4 %, When the SOV table is generated, Then they show « ~0% », « ~0% » and « 12% »
**TAC5** — Given 48 SOV rows and 10 ranking rows, When the sheet is generated, Then the next section (sources) starts below the row of the 48th brand and no cell of the ranking table is lost
**TAC6** — Given a category sheet, When it is generated, Then it has the same two tables for the category scope; the Other category sheet has no SOV table
**TAC7** — Given an unbranded workbook, When it is generated, Then the landscape ranking table and the SOV table are both on the overview sheet and on each category sheet
**TAC8** — Given a French or Spanish export, When the SOV table is generated, Then its title and header read « Part de voix » / « Part de voix % » or « Cuota de voz » / « Cuota de voz % »
**TAC9** — Given an empty distribution, When the sheet is generated, Then there is no SOV table, the ranking table is unchanged and no exception is raised
**TAC10** — Given another organisation's report, When it is exported, Then the export still returns 404 (the distribution call is scoped by organisation)

**TAC11** — (PM 2026-11-10) Given a scope with 120 brands, When the SOV table is generated, Then it has 100 brand rows (rank 1..100) then « and 20 more brands » in column G (one cell, H–I empty), and the next section starts below that row; 101 brands → « and 1 more brand »; 100 brands or fewer → no such row (N counts every brand of the scope, the slices included); FR « et N autres marques », ES « y N marcas más »

**TAC12** — (PM 2026-11-10, 875646) Given a scope with 26,491 brands, When the SOV table is generated, Then the last row reads EN « and 26,391 more brands », FR « et 26 391 autres marques », ES « y 26.391 marcas más »; numbers from 1,000 to 9,999 are grouped the same way as in the tooltip (« y 1.417 marcas más »)

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Backend only. The Share of Voice table reads the same data as the dashboard donut (whole period). The ranking table, like the app, shows the last analysis date of the period, ordered by Visibility %. Whole numbers, « ~0% » under 0.5 % (the Figma frames show one decimal, the epic rules it out). When the Share of Voice table is longer than the ranking table, the next section starts below it. Data from STORY-51.4. Design: GEO-1543 (flow 2).

technicalNotes.heading: Code review (2026-11-10)
technicalNotes.text: Second review of the « first 100 brands » change: no functional defect. TAC11 corrected (101 brands, not 91, give « and 1 more brand »), tests added at the 100 / 101 boundary, Javadoc repaired. Two product questions asked on GEO-1537 and answered the same day (875646): thousands separator added (TAC12, reviewed, no defect), tracked brand beyond rank 100 kept as is. Still to check by hand: open an export in Excel and LibreOffice.

**Others line:** Given the donut shows an Others slice, When the line is drawn, Then it sits under the chips, centred, 675 pt wide, 7 pt text, 10.5 pt line height, slate-500, 2 lines at most, with the lead « Others 58%: » in bold

**Unbranded (frame 3.2):** Given an unbranded deck, When its Share of Voice slide is drawn, Then it shows the same chip and line under its donut, with no « and N more » part when Others holds 10 brands or fewer

**TAC1** — Given an export with or without a period, When the overview and category donuts are fetched, Then the distribution is read with the dashboard's scope: the period's snapshots and period key (else the anchor snapshot alone), the category, the markets and the AI engines

**TAC2** — Given the tracked brand is outside the top 10, When the KPI slide is drawn, Then it is not added to the slices and the centre still shows the entity name and the Share of Voice KPI of the period

**TAC4** — Given 6 brands in Others, When the line is computed, Then all 6 are listed with no « more » part; Given 11 brands that all fit, Then 10 are listed + « and 1 more brand, see the Excel export »

**TAC10** — Given a branded KPI slide with an Others line and a 2-row legend, with and without the evolution pill, When it is drawn, Then the pill and the name and value texts are inside the donut hole, the line ends inside the card, and the centre value is the Share of Voice KPI of the period

**TAC11** — (PM 2026-11-10, 875646) Given 1,427 brands behind Others, When the line is computed, Then it ends with « and 1,417 more brands, see the Excel export » (FR « et 1 417 autres marques, voir l'export Excel », ES « y 1.417 marcas más, ver la exportación de Excel ») and still fits on 2 lines; the number is never split across the two lines

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Backend only; the PDF is the deck rendered, so it follows. Every deck donut (overview and category KPI slides, Share of Voice slide of an unbranded deck) uses the dashboard's data; the tracked brand is no longer forced into the slices. The hole shows the Share of Voice of the whole period, as the dashboard. Whole numbers (the Figma frames show one decimal). Data from STORY-51.4. Design: GEO-1543 (flow 3).

technicalNotes.heading: Implementation notes (2026-11-09)
technicalNotes.text:
- The Others slice follows the dashboard as shipped by STORY-51.1: its size and its display threshold (> 0.05) use the summed Share of Voice of the brands behind Others.
- With a 3-row legend the donut hole keeps at least 42 pt and the ring thins (6 pt minimum); when the Others line is drawn the legend keeps 3 rows at most, longer brand names cut with « … ».
- **Code review:** Chinese and Japanese brand names are measured in the font they are drawn with, so the Others line stays on 2 lines for them too (they could take a third line before the fix); a long entity name in the hole is cut with « … » so it never wraps; the « Others » chip itself is never cut.
- **Cost check on staging:** Toyota (QA-GEO), « All reports » (147 snapshots, 2 categories): the deck adds about 1.6 s with a cold cache and about nothing once the dashboard donut was opened; today's PowerPoint takes 114 s on the server because of the Time Evolution slides (bug GEO-1591, not this story), the PDF adds 3 s of rendering.

technicalAcceptanceCriteria.text: **TAC1** — With 15 brand families named in scope, the response has 10 `brands` and `others.brandCount = 5`, `others.brands` the 5 others in order; `Σ brands.sov + others.sov = 100` within rounding (± 0.01 per brand).

**TAC2** — With 10 families or fewer, all ≥ 0.5 %, `others` is absent from the response. With one family outside the slices at 0.03 %, `others` is present (the Excel export lists it) even though the donut draws no Others slice under 0.05 % — STORY-51.1 hides the tooltip in that case.
**TAC3** — A family at 0.4 % ranked 9th by value is not in `brands` but is in `others.brands`; a family at an exact 0.496 % (0.50 rounded to 2 decimals) stays a slice.

**TAC4** — Two families with the same exact Share of Voice come out « Alpha » before « beta » (case-insensitive), in `brands` and in `others.brands`. With 12 families at the same exact Share of Voice, the first 10 by name are the slices and the last 2 are in `others.brands`.
**TAC5** — No family named in scope → `brands = []`, no `others` (today's empty case unchanged).

**TAC6** — `isTargetBrand` is set on the tracked brand wherever it lands (slice or Others); unbranded analyses never set it. Matching is unchanged and the same as Brand Rankings (containment), so on the full list more than one family can carry `isTargetBrand = true`; STORY-51.2 decides how it highlights them.
**TAC7** — Cross-tenant: the Share of Voice distribution requested with another organisation's id returns 404 (new service test).
**TAC8** — The export scope gives the distribution the same snapshot ids and period key as the dashboard endpoint, with and without a period.

technicalNotes.heading: Scope note
technicalNotes.text: Backend shared foundation of the epic, no Jira user story of its own (the epic's « Dependencies »: the full brand list behind Others). Almost no visible change: same slices and same Others slice, except between brands with exactly the same Share of Voice, whose order can change (A to Z), and, when the 10th and 11th brands tie, which one is the 10th slice. Depends on GEO-1556 (story 50.7b, done). Blocks STORY-51.1, STORY-51.2 and STORY-51.3. Design reference: GEO-1543 (rationale D2).
